problems.stem: What is the main purpose of formative evaluation?
options: To judge final impact only after the course is complete
To catch design problems during development so revisions can still be made
To replace learner testing with SME opinion only
To measure ROI after six months of implementation
problems.explanation: Formative evaluation happens during design and development so teams can improve the instruction before launch.

problems.stem: Which Kirkpatrick level asks whether learners actually acquired knowledge or skill?
problems.explanation: Level 2 focuses on whether learning occurred, typically through tests, demonstrations, or performance evidence.

problems.stem: Why is a high post-course satisfaction score not enough to prove instructional effectiveness?
options: Because reaction data can be positive even when real learning or transfer is weak
Because satisfaction surveys are illegal in most settings
Because reaction data always measures ROI directly
Because only psychometricians can collect learner feedback
problems.explanation: Learners may enjoy a course without learning much. Reaction data is useful, but it does not prove performance improvement by itself.

problems.stem: Which evidence source best aligns with Level 3 behavior evaluation?
options: A smile-sheet rating gathered immediately after class
A pre/post knowledge quiz taken in the LMS
Observation of whether employees changed their on-the-job behavior after training
A brand-style review of the course visuals
problems.explanation: Level 3 asks whether the learner changed behavior in practice, not just whether they liked the course or passed a quiz.
